title: The Three Zones: Evil Bound Within Good Bound Within Divine Governance
arc: When the Living Spirit built the cosmos he hung three concentric Zones, one within another: the innermost girdle contains the five powers of Darkness as captives; the middle girdle is the Five Sons of the First Man who hold those powers fettered within themselves; and the outermost girdle is the firmament above, where the great ruling presence sustains the whole structure of the cosmos.
reading:
This chapter is a piece of cosmic architecture told through a single image: the Zone, the cosmic girdle of states. The teaching's claim is that the cosmos as we now know it is not one belt but three belts nested inside one another, and that this nesting is itself the meaning of redemption-in-progress. The Living Spirit, the operative Divine power that builds order in receptive states, is named at the outset as the builder. When he "established the worlds, he hung the Zones, a Zone within another Zone again." Building, here, is not making something new from nothing; it is the act of binding what is already chaotic into ordered concentric containment.

The first and innermost Zone is identified as "the five powers of the Darkness, of the males and the females" — that is, the Five Worlds of Darkness, the complete five-fold structure of self-love in both its active and receptive modes. In the correspondential reading, this is the proprium in its full articulation: every mode by which self-love expresses itself, gathered and enclosed. The teaching is careful to say that this innermost belt does not stand free. It is hung within another Zone, and that second Zone is the five heaven-men, the Five Sons of the First Man — the five attributes of Divine Truth descending as the Living Soul. The reason for the nesting is given plainly: "all the enmity is fettered, reckoned within them within." Enmity, the cosmic principle of opposition to the Lord, is not destroyed; it is held captive inside the Five Sons. The very body of the descended Divine Truth is now the prison-belt around the powers of Darkness. This is the first great teaching of the chapter: in the present cosmic state, evil exists only as something fettered inside good, accounted for and held within the Living Soul.

The text then names a further, outer Zone — the Zone of the firmament that is above, in which "the great" one (the surviving fragments point to the Great Builder or King of Honor, the Lord governing the heavens of the natural) presides, and from which "the whole structure is hung." This is the third Zone of the cosmos. So the architecture stands complete: at the center, the bound darkness; surrounding it, the Five Sons of the First Man as living girdle; surrounding them, the firmament-Zone where the divine ruling presence holds the entire suspended structure in its place. Each inner state is contained by a higher state, and the highest is contained by the Lord himself.

Spiritually, this is a teaching about how the Lord governs the mingled state. Falsity-from-evil is real, but it is never sovereign; it is always interior to a containing truth, which is always interior to a containing divine government. The cosmos is not a battlefield of equals — it is a series of concentric custodies. The proprium with all its five powers is fettered within the descended Divine Human; the descended Divine Human is hung within the firmament where Divine Truth rules. Read inwardly, this is the structure of every regenerate person under the Lord's providence: the loves of self are not abolished but bound, held within the spiritual mind formed by the Lord, which is itself held within the ruling truth of heaven. Read outwardly, it is the structure of the whole cosmos as the present arena of redemption. The lacunae obscure the precise naming of the third Zone's occupant, but the surviving sequence — Darkness fettered, Sons of the First Man holding it, firmament above sustaining all — is unmistakable: the cosmos is built as a triple containment, and that triple containment is itself the work by which the Living Spirit prepares the mingled world for its eventual sorting.
